newsitem.title: USA: ENOVA, Pacific Enterprises to buy trading firm.
newsitem.headline: ENOVA, Pacific Enterprises to buy trading firm.

text.p: Enova Corp. and Pacific Enterprises said Thursday they would pay $190 million to acquire AIG Trading Corp. in a move that links the giant California power suppliers to an energy trading firm.
The utilities, which have agreed to merge, will each pay half the purchase price and acquire all of AIG Trading's outstanding common stock.
The acquisition of AIG, one of the nation's leading natural gas and power marketers, comes as the U.S. utiilty industry is being deregulated, heightening competition for power customers.

In June, Enova and Pacific Enterprises won preliminary approval from the government to merge in a $2.5 billion deal, creating the nation's largest U.S. utility in terms of customers. The merger is expected to be completed early next year, subject to approval by the state of California.
Pacific Enterprise is the parent company of Southern California Gas Co., known as SoCal Gas. Enova's main subsidiary is San Diego Gas & Electric Co.
The merger gives Connecticut-based AIG Trading access to the utilities' massive power generation and transmission resources.
"This transaction establishes the wholesale commodity trading business necessary to support our retail marketing," said Stephen Baum, chief executive officer of Enova.
"Now we will have a full portfolio of energy services for our customers," he said.
AIG Trading is a subsidiary American International Group, the New York-based insurance company.
The acquisition, which is subject to the approval of the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission, is expected to be completed by year-end.
